The printed group is Gamma (GX.printedGamma2_eq_top); DEC-58's normal closure is refuted and kept as the record

hypotheses.paper: 'the fibre above (0,0) in Y_2 is a Cantor set'
hypotheses.note: for Gamma_2': GX.absGal_Y₂_fiber_cantor_corrected (fibre homeomorphic to {0,1}^N, GX.cantFiberHomeo, hence to cantorSet). Record: for the normal closure it is false, not compact (GX.absGal_Y₂_fiber_not_cantor_simple), infinite and totally disconnected (GX.absGal_Y₂_fiber_corrected_simple)
DEC-68 (e): lollipop loops GX.absGalSimpleLoop, used only by the recorded counterexample; Gamma_2' is defined by windings and needs no gamma_n
DEC-55 literal reading: GX.absGal_not_isSLSCInCC in GX.absolute_galois_corrected
bibliographic remark, not a mathematical assertion of the example

findings: l.1571, first claim, proved in the literal reading (DEC-55): C minus S is not semi-locally simply connected in C (GX.absGal_not_isSLSCInCC).

l.1572-1573 as printed is refuted (record, DEC-69): the printed Gamma_2 is Gamma; for the normal closure of the squares of the (lollipop) simple loops the fibre over 0 is not compact (GX.absGal_Y₂_fiber_not_cantor_simple).

l.1572-1573 corrected (DEC-69), PROVED sorry-free: for Gamma_2' = kernel of the mod-2 windings around the 1/n the fibre above (0,0) of Y_2' is a Cantor set (GX.absGal_Y₂_fiber_cantor_corrected). Proof: square roots s_n of p - 1/(n+1) on the universal cover; deck signs eps_n = (-1)^winding; over D_k the components of the preimage are exactly the 2^k sign classes of sigma_0..sigma_{k-1} (GX.cantZ_comp), the hard half realising every eventually constant sign pattern (eventual constancy: a loop stays away from 0, GX.cant_eps_eventually) by small circles around the 1/(n+1), n >= k, and the circle of radius R_k around 0, inside D_k; ends over 0 = sign sequences, a continuous bijection from the compact {0,1}^N onto the Hausdorff fibre.

l.1573: 'This answers positively Problem 10.7 of MR2198590' is bibliographic and not formalized; with the corrected Gamma_2' the example does exhibit a Cantor fibre over a point of the branching locus.
questions: Is the bibliographic sentence 'answers positively Problem 10.7 of MR2198590' (l.1573) outside the row's certification, as taken here (row closed under DEC-69)? If the master reads it as an assertion, downgrade to partial.

labels.label: ex:wild_cantor_general_antoine

hypotheses.paper: S a wild Cantor set [general_antoine] in S^3
hypotheses.note: DEC-58, DEC-68 (f): ONE explicit Antoine necklace GX.antoineNecklace, built and proved a Cantor set (GX.antoineNecklace_isCantorSubset, sorry-free); the claim GX.antoineNecklace_wild_not_isSLSCInCC is stated for it

hypotheses.paper: (cited, general_antoine) Antoine's theorem: the necklace is wild, its complement not simply connected / meridians essential
hypotheses.note: GX.antoineNecklace_antoine, the only sorry of the file (residual named in its tag)
DEC-55: literal and homotopy forms agree for closed C in S^3 (GX.sphere3_isSLSCInCC_compl_iff)

sorries.obstruction: Antoine's theorem for the explicit necklace. Residual, exactly: (1) a meridian of a first-generation (or generation-n) link L is not null-homotopic in S^3 minus (C ∩ L) — no abelian invariant can detect it (Alexander duality: H^1 of the complement of a closed subset of a Cantor set vanishes, so windings, linking numbers, maps to S^1 and abelian covers give 0; the Z/2-valued/abelian covering route of the dispatch therefore cannot work as such), and by compactness of a null-homotopy one must detect it in the complement of every finite stage (64^(m-n) linked PL solid tori), which needs for every m a non-abelian covering (an (m-n)-fold iterated lift) or Antoine's van Kampen computation; mathlib has no van Kampen theorem, no pi_1 of a solid-torus complement and no PL solid-torus theory; (2) accessibility: a path from each x ∈ C to the meridian meeting C only at x; (3) wildness: S^3 minus a Cantor subset of a great circle is simply connected (a general-position/van Kampen argument), which with (1)-(2) excludes tameness via GX.isSLSCIn_compl_of_simplyConnected.

findings: Under DEC-58/DEC-68 (f) the example is about one explicit Antoine necklace, constructed and proved a Cantor set; the general wild-Cantor reading fails as soon as some wild Cantor set has simply connected, locally non-separating complement (GX.wild_cantor_claim_false_of_exists, proved).

kb_proposals: Abelian quotients of pi_1 of a planar complement through continuous square roots: lift p - a through exp on the universal cover (IsCoveringMap.existsUnique_continuousMap_lifts with Complex.isCoveringMap_exp), s = exp(l/2); deck transformations act by eps = (-1)^winding (GX.cantEps_fromPath via GX.cantSq_liftFrom_loop + GX.absGal_deckHom_base); the kernel is a Subgroup defined by eps = 1 (GX.cantGamma).

Fibres of Fox completions as Cantor spaces: show the components of the preimage of each basic disc are exactly the sign classes (locally constant Bool invariant + a realisation lemma for the hard half), build ends as FiberThread.toEnd over range fibD, then Continuous.homeoOfEquivCompactToT2 from (ℕ → Bool) and cantorSetHomeomorphNatToBool.

Universal cover: two points over the same point differ by a deck transformation (GX.cant_exists_deck: g = (fromPath (cls'.trans cls.symm))⁻¹); deck maps permute components of preimages (GX.cant_deck_image_comp, Homeomorph.image_connectedComponentIn).
Inside rw, a Decidable instance depending on the rewritten term breaks the motive (decide (x * y = 1)); use simp only instead.
In ∀-statements with instance binders, prove by `intro n hn Y _ _ S hS` in tactic mode rather than a term-mode fun, which mis-assigns binders.
